title: Dates go past 9999 and before 0001; `DATEADD` wraps at 2^31 days
verdict: computes years 0 to 302024 and negative ones; `DATEADD(DAY, 2^31 - 1, …)` wraps (SF-3)
description: `DATEADD(DAY, 1, '9999-12-31')` is `10000-01-01` and `DATEADD(DAY, -1, '0001-01-01')` `0000-12-31`; `DATEADD(YEAR, 300000, '2024-01-01')` is year 302024; text casts accept `'10000-01-01'` and `'-0001-01-01'`. Timestamps go past both ends too. Such values break clients: the Python connector cannot convert them, so the probes print them with `TO_VARCHAR`.
`DATEADD(DAY, 2147483647, '2024-01-01')` is `-5877587-06-21`: the day count wraps at 32 bits, silently. See [SF-3](../../../upstream/bugs/SF-3.json).
reference: `date_range`: arithmetic raises outside 0001-01-01 … 9999-12-31. sverify refuses literals outside years 1 to 9999 and its SQL range-checks computed dates and timestamps (the shared lowering's checks of the years chrono represents), so a wrapped result raises too.

provenance.checked_by: sverify_dev.probe_snowflake through the Snowflake CLI (Snowflake characterization session)

evidence.sql: SELECT to_varchar(dateadd(DAY, -1, a)), to_varchar(dateadd(DAY, 1, b)), to_varchar(dateadd(YEAR, 1, b)), SYSTEM$TYPEOF(dateadd(DAY, 1, b)) FROM (VALUES ('0001-01-01'::DATE, '9999-12-31'::DATE)) AS s(a, b)

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_snowflake` runs each query through `snow sql` (Snowflake CLI 3.32.1) on an X-Small warehouse, Snowflake 10.40.102, with the session's `TIMEZONE` set to UTC and `USE_CACHED_RESULT` off; every other parameter is the account's default, recorded in the header of probes.json (`WEEK_START` 0, `WEEK_OF_YEAR_POLICY` 0, `DEFAULT_NULL_ORDERING` LAST, `TIMESTAMP_TYPE_MAPPING` TIMESTAMP_NTZ). The inputs are literal `VALUES`, except the `sample-*` probes, which read TPC-H's LINEITEM (6,001,215 rows) in SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA.
